found.summary: The transcriptions match the PDFs, and both PDFs contain the same layer. Both scripts run on CPU and print the same thing every time: Blueprint gives Test 1 PASSED and 149.66 MB, Replacement gives a pass and 42.234 MB. Neither test checks what it claims. Test 1 never produces a single subnormal value: at log σ0 = −15 or −12 every value is a normal float32. In that state the layer attends only to the current token, and the same test also passes at the default σ0. Test 2 compares 149.66 MB, counted without deduplication, against ~158 MB, which was counted by bench.py with deduplication. Counted the same way, v2 saves 15–17% less than v1, and it saves 3.6× more than naive softmax. v1's 158 MB never included the grid. The grid cost was in temporary memory, which this test does not measure; there v2 really is about 3.7× lower than v1 (peak RSS). The specific v1 NaN mechanism (abs on subnormal values) is gone. But v2 has new NaN boundaries: at log σ0 ≤ −23.75 log_sigma0.grad becomes NaN, and at log σ0 ≥ 44.5 everything does. Blueprint's Test 1 recipe (T=128) would have caught v1's NaN. Replacement's recipe (T=64) would not.

findings.claim: src/paper_v2_blueprint.py and src/paper_v2_replacement.py are faithful transcriptions of the two v2 PDFs
findings.evidence: PDF text was extracted with PDFKit and compared after removing whitespace (and '_' for the Replacement PDF, whose text layer splits underscores). Lengths are identical: 3620 = 3620 chars and 4802 = 4802 chars. Every remaining difference is a move pair caused by extraction order, e.g. 'sigma0))**2' moved, 'mask=True):' moved. All 8 pages were rendered to PNG and checked visually; no difference changes behaviour. In the PDF, wrapped lines such as the third banner print( in the Replacement appear at column 0. These are display wraps, and the transcription indents them correctly.

findings.claim: Both PDFs contain the same AnalyticalCVQIAALayer
findings.evidence: With docstrings removed, the ASTs differ in one place only: Blueprint's `return self.out_proj(out.transpose(1,2).contiguous().view(B,T,C))` is split into two statements in Replacement. With shared weights and random log_sigma0 in [-3,3] over 3 seeds, the differences in outputs, x.grad and parameter grads are all exactly 0. 99,076 parameters at d=128, H=4.

findings.claim: The authors' verification scripts run and pass
findings.evidence: 5 runs each on CPU. Blueprint prints 'Test 1 (CPU Gradient Stability): PASSED (0 NaNs found)' and 'Test 2 (Saved Autograd Tensors at Context 512): 149.66 MB' every run; it has no seed, but the byte count depends only on tensor shapes. Replacement prints 'Test Passed. Absolute stability achieved on CPU', '42.234 MB' and 'Grid-free O(T^2) execution confirmed' every run. That last status line is an unconditional print with no check behind it. Replacement creates AdamW but never calls step(), so its 'integration suite' trains nothing.

findings.claim: Test 1 'explicitly force[s] parameters into subnormal bounds' (Blueprint, log_sigma0=-15); 'Non-Zero Subnormal Stability' (Replacement, -12)
findings.evidence: At -15 (σ0=3.06e-7, σ0²=9.4e-14), all values stay normal. Envelope on the diagonal is 0.01368; the formula gives √2, but the +1e-9 in the denominator dominates. Envelope off the diagonal runs from 1.32e-13 (dt=1) to 1.04e-15 (dt=127). A off the diagonal runs from 3.4e-35 to 1.3e-25, all above the float32 normal minimum 1.18e-38. Over 50 seeds there are 0 subnormal values in any intermediate, in their grads, or in parameter and input grads. At -12 (Replacement), A off the diagonal runs from 3.9e-28 to 1.4e-20, again with 0 subnormals. Sweep (seed 0): subnormals first appear at log σ0=-18 (112 values), then -20 (75,332) and -22 (129,738).

findings.claim: Test 1 checks gradient stability of the attention layer
findings.evidence: In the forced state the layer only copies each token's own value; there is no cross-token attention. At -15 over 50 seeds, the largest weight on any other token is 4.6e-18. Row sums of A_normalized drop as low as 0.080: the diagonal A goes down to 1.3e-9, comparable to the +1e-9 in the normalisation, and 55 of 51,200 rows sum to less than 0.99. At -12 (Replacement), max|y − out_proj(V_own)| = 2.4e-6 against |y| ≤ 1.13. The same Test 1 recipe also passes at the default log σ0 = log 2 (0 NaN tensors), so forcing σ0 adds nothing. The test does confirm finite gradients, but only for a non-attending layer.

findings.claim: Would the same kind of test have caught the v1 NaN?
findings.evidence: Blueprint's recipe (B=2, T=128, C=64, CPU, sum().backward(), isnan on grads) applied to v1 from wavellm_fixed.py, with positions 0.1·index: 10 of 34 parameter tensors and x.grad are NaN in 5 of 5 seeds. Also at B=4, T=128, C=128. So a Blueprint-style test would have caught v1. Replacement's recipe uses T=64, where v1 has 0/34 NaN at C=64 and C=128 over 5 seeds; v1's first NaN appears between T=93 and T=96. So Replacement's Test 1 cannot tell v1 from v2. v1's NaN depends on T, not on any parameter: at T=128 its narrow-head overlaps include 21 subnormal and 62 exactly zero causal pairs. Forcing σ0 is therefore unrelated to catching it.

findings.claim: 'CPU NaNs Fixed: We eliminated the torch.abs() derivative singularity'
findings.evidence: The abs mechanism is gone. At log σ0 between -18 and -22 there are up to 129,738 subnormal values in the forward pass and 0 NaN, so Re²+Im² handles them. New boundaries exist, though. At log σ0 ≤ -23.75, log_sigma0.grad is NaN (5/5 seeds; at -23.5, 0/5). The cause: the sqrt argument 2σ0²/(σt²+1e-9) underflows to exactly 0 (1,326 causal pairs at -24, 6,903 at -25), and the sqrt gradient becomes inf·0. At log σ0 ≥ 44.5, σ0² overflows, and all 16,384 outputs and all 12 parameter grads are NaN. At log σ0 ≤ -25, attention row sums go to 0 and the layer outputs only the bias. Whether training can reach these values was not tested; from the init value 0.69 it would take a drift of more than 24.

findings.claim: Test 2 tracks saved tensors 'exactly like cv-qiaa-eval hooks'; 149.66 MB vs '~158 MB' for the old implementation
findings.evidence: Blueprint's hook does not deduplicate. At T=512, v2 makes 45 pack calls on 37 distinct tensors, so 16.00 MB is counted twice. bench.py deduplicates by (data_ptr, dtype, shape). Wrapping backward adds 0 pack calls (45 forward = 45 forward+backward). Recount at B=4, D=128, H=4, T=512, authors' method / bench method: v1 180.23 / 158.21 (bench.json gives 158.21); v2 149.66 / 133.66; naive softmax 37.75 / 37.62; born 54.53 / 54.41; sdpa 6.53 / 6.41. The letter puts 149.66 (no dedup) next to 158 (dedup). Counted the same way, the reduction is 17.0% (authors' method) or 15.5% (bench method). By bench method v2 is 3.55× naive softmax, 2.46× born and 20.9× sdpa. Bench method at other lengths: T=256 v2 36.45 vs v1 46.19; T=1024 v2 511.44 vs v1 580.25.

findings.claim: 'The old implementation required ~158 MB at this scale due to grid generation'
findings.evidence: v1's 158.21 MB of saved tensors at T=512 contains no grid tensor. Contents: 12 complex64 tensors (4,512,512) = 96 MB, 8 float32 tensors (4,512,512) = 32 MB, 60 tensors (4,512,32) = 15 MB, and so on. No 4-D tensor has the grid dimension 64. x_grid.requires_grad and positions.requires_grad are both False, so the grid computation is outside autograd. The grid cost was in temporary memory, which Test 2 does not measure. Peak RSS growth for one forward+backward in a fresh process: T=512, v1 882 MB vs v2 229–240 MB; T=1024, v1 3,210 MB vs v2 843 MB. So the real gain is about 3.7× in peak memory, not in saved tensors. Naive softmax is 53–81 MB and sdpa 29 MB at T=512; RSS is noisy because the machine's load average was about 106.

findings.claim: 'The layer now runs at computational parity with standard matrix attention'
findings.evidence: Saved memory at T=512 (bench method): v2 133.66 MB vs naive softmax 37.62 MB (3.55×) and sdpa 6.41 MB. Peak RSS growth at T=512: v2 229–240 MB vs naive 53–81 MB; at T=1024, 843 vs 222 MB. CPU time could not be measured reliably (load average about 106): at T=512, v2 took 276–807 ms vs naive softmax 206–228 ms over 3 repeats, so the time result is unsettled.

findings.claim: Replacement Test 2: '42.234 MB ... Grid-free O(T^2) execution confirmed'
findings.evidence: The test counts the whole demo model (embedding, layer, lm_head, cross-entropy) at T=256, vocab 32, with no baseline and an unconditional status line. It runs with log_sigma0 still at -12 from Test 1, which does not change the byte count. Breakdown: authors' method 42.234 MB, of which the layer alone is 41.461; bench method 37.109 for the model and 36.461 for the layer. Saved memory is O(T²): 36.45 → 133.66 → 511.44 MB (×3.67, ×3.83). But v1's saved memory was also O(T²): 46.19 → 158.21 → 580.25. So this metric cannot show 'grid-free'.

checks.correction: Refuted. Both tests do produce subnormal values. The previous check counted only 5 named tensors and their .grad (test1_seeds.py / sweep_sigma.py). It missed the squared terms Psi_re**2 and Psi_im**2, and all backward gradients along the sigma path. Corrected statement: log σ0 = -15 does not make any parameter subnormal (σ0 = 3.06e-7 is a normal float). The envelope, A, the row sums and A_normalized also stay normal. But the forward squared terms contain about 8 subnormals per run, and the backward gradient with respect to sigma_t_sq is roughly 20% subnormal. All of this passes without NaN. So the tests do exercise subnormal arithmetic, but only on a path where no singular operation follows. They never reach the actual v2 failure point: underflow of the sqrt argument, at log σ0 ≤ -23.75 for T=128.
checks.evidence: allops.py hooks every aten op output, forward and backward, via TorchDispatchMode (seed 0, B,T,C = 2,128,64). Subnormals per log σ0 (fwd / bwd): 0.69: 0/0; -6: 0/0; -8: 0/68; -10: 0/56,635; -12: 0/31,507; -15: 7/43,772; -18: 3,325/0. The first subnormals therefore appear at -8, not -18. t1_state.py, over 50 seeds at -15: Psi_re**2 has 201 subnormals and Psi_im**2 has 197; A, env and A_normalized have 0. t1_grads2.py, Blueprint recipe at -15, seed 0: DivBackward0 input slot 1 (gradient with respect to sigma_t_sq+1e-9) has 13,460 of 65,536 values subnormal, and the following AddBackward nodes have 13,460 each. The Replacement recipe exactly as published (seed 42, -12) has 3,632 of 16,384 subnormal, plus 636 in the exp-argument denominator gradient. Both runs end with 0 NaN. CPU keeps subnormals: 1e-40*1.0 = 9.99e-41.

v1_recipe.py, v1 from wavellm_fixed with positions 0.1*index. At B,T,C = 2,128,64: 10 of 34 parameter tensors NaN and x.grad NaN in 5 of 5 seeds. At T=64 with C=64 or C=128: 0 of 34 in 5 of 5 seeds. The first T with NaN is 94 for seeds 0, 1 and 2. A one-layer v1 WaveLLM at B=2, T=64 gives 0 NaN in 3 of 3 seeds. In the narrow head (σ0 = 0.5) at T=128, of 8,256 causal pairs, 21 overlaps are subnormal and 62 are exactly 0. These overlaps do not depend on any parameter.

checks.correction: The mechanism and the -23.75 boundary hold, but four details need correcting. (1) The upper boundary is log σ0 > 44.017, not ≥ 44.5. At that point 2.0*sigma0**2 overflows (ln sqrt(FLT_MAX/2) = 44.017), and σ0² itself overflows above 44.36. The previous sweep jumped from 44 to 44.5. (2) The lower boundary depends on T. The sqrt argument is about 2σ0⁴/dt² and becomes 0 once σ0 < (0.35e-45·(T-1)²)^(1/4). That gives -23.75 at T=128, about -23.05 at T=512 and about -24.1 at T=64. (3) The forward subnormal counts are undercounts: counting all ops at -22 gives 289,335 forward and 64,544 backward. (4) At -25 the row sums are about 1e-4 (median 1.15e-4, max 1.7e-3), not 0. The output equals the bias up to 9.4e-4, against max|y| = 0.125. At -30 it equals the bias up to 5e-8. Also, in PyTorch the NaN arises in the sqrt backward as 0/0 (a div op), which is mathematically the same as inf·0.
checks.evidence: allops.py: at 44.01 everything is finite; at 44.02 the first non-finite value is in the forward mul of shape (1,4,1,1), and all 16,384 outputs and all 12 grads are non-finite. At 44.4 the first non-finite op is pow. misc.py over 5 seeds at T=128: -23.74 gives 0/5 NaN and -23.75 gives 5/5, and only log_sigma0 is NaN, never x.grad. At T=512: -23.1 gives NaN, -23.0 does not. At T=64: -24.1 gives NaN, -23.1 does not. The first non-finite op at -23.75 is a backward aten.div of shape (1,4,128,128).

In the asymptotic sense it is true against naive matrix attention: both are O(T²) memory and O(T²·d) time. Against sdpa it is not, because sdpa's saved memory grows linearly (3.33 → 6.41 → 12.56 MB). found.summary: The v2 envelope formula is not a wave-packet overlap in any of the three natural cases: (a) a spread packet against an unspread one, (b) both packets spread, chirp included, (c) the v1 paper's own formula. At d=0 it equals √2, while a normalised overlap never exceeds 1; identically E = √2·(σ0/σt)·(c)². The spreading law σ(t) is correct. But the overlap of two packets that evolved for the same time does not depend on t by unitarity: it is a static Gaussian kernel, and the “dispersion” in the v1 formula appeared only because the chirp phase was dropped. In ML terms the positional part of v2 is a fixed monotonic distance prior with one learnable σ0 per head. It is exactly a softmax of the logits 2·log|q·k*| plus a bias b(d): quadratic nearby, logarithmic far away (weight ~1/d²). It does not resemble ALiBi; at σ0≤2 it is close to the KERPLE log kernel. The v1 phase encoding e^{iωs} is absent from v2 altogether. Head behaviour disagrees with Annex A: at small σ0 a head looks almost entirely at its own token and has a long power-law tail, at σ0=4–5 it is a window of 2–3 tokens, and a wide window appears only at σ0≳20, where it is an ordinary Gaussian window unaffected by dispersion.

findings.claim: The v2 letter: “deriving the closed-form analytical coordinate-space integral of the wave-packet overlaps”; in the code E = sqrt(2σ0²/σt²)·exp(−dt²/(2σt²)), σt² = σ0² + (ħ·dt/(m·σ0))².
findings.evidence:
The paper's conventions (v1 section 2.2): ψ0 = (πσ0²)^(−1/4)·exp(−(x−a)²/2σ0²), ħ = m = 1, τ = t/σ0². Solution of the free Schrödinger equation: ψ(x,t) = (πσ0²)^(−1/4)·(1+iτ)^(−1/2)·exp(−(x−a)²/(2σ0²(1+iτ))) = (πσt²)^(−1/4)·e^{−i·atanτ/2}·exp(−(1−iτ)(x−a)²/2σt²), where σt² = σ0²(1+τ²); the second factor with (1−iτ) is the chirp. We use ∫exp(−α(x−a)²−β(x−b)²)dx = sqrt(π/(α+β))·exp(−αβd²/(α+β)).
(a) An unspread packet at d against a packet spread over t=d: α=1/2σ0², β=1/(2σ0²(1+iτ)), hence I_a = sqrt(2/(2+iτ))·exp(−d²/(2σ0²(2+iτ))) and |I_a| = (4/(4+τ²))^{1/4}·exp(−d²/(σ0²(4+τ²))).
(b) Both packets spread over the same t, chirp included: α=(1+iτ)/2σt², β=(1−iτ)/2σt², hence overlap = exp(−d²/4σ0²).
(c) The paper's formula is (b) without the chirp: exp(−d²/4σt²).
Quadrature with up to 4·10^5 points against these formulas for σ0∈{0.3,1,2,5,20} and d∈{0,…,1000} gives a maximum error of 9.4e−16 for (a), 4.4e−16 for (b), 2.2e−16 for (c).
The code matches none of the cases. At σ0=2: for d=5 |a|=0.299, b=0.210, c=0.543, code 0.261; for d=100 |a|=5.3e−3, b=4e−272, c=0.368, code 7.7e−3.
E(0)=√2=1.414 for any σ0, although any normalised overlap is at most 1 (Cauchy–Schwarz; for real Gaussians the prefactor sqrt(2σ1σ2/(σ1²+σ2²)) ≤ 1). E>1 for d≤1 (σ0=2), d≤4 (σ0=5), d≤16 (σ0=20).
Identity with error ≤2.2e−16: E = √2·(σ0/σt)·[c]². The exponent is twice that of the paper's formula, and a factor σ0/σt is added. E/√2 equals the density ratio N(d;0,σt²)/N(0;0,σ0²); in the PDF the line is labelled “continuous spatial envelope density”. That is a density, not an overlap amplitude, and the Born rule then squares it once more.

findings.claim: v1, section 2.2: the overlap exp(−(sQ−sK)²/4σ(t)²) widens with dt and removes the limitation “static Gaussian kernels choke out long-range context”.
findings.evidence: If both packets evolve for the same time t, the overlap is preserved by unitarity: <U(t)ψa|U(t)ψb> = <ψa|ψb> = exp(−d²/4σ0²). This is a static Gaussian kernel with no t in it. Analytically: in case (b) αβ/(α+β) = (1+τ²)/(4σt²) = 1/(4σ0²), and the prefactor is 1. Quadrature agrees to 4.4e−16. The paper's formula arises only if the chirp phase exp(iτ(x−a)²/2σt²) of the spread packet is thrown away. In case (a) the chirp is included, and the tail at large d is |I_a| ≈ sqrt(2σ0²/d)·e^{−σ0²}, i.e. it decays as d^(−1/2). Formula (c) instead has a plateau e^{−σ0²/4}: for example, 0.978 at σ0=0.3 at any d.

findings.claim: σ(t) = σ0·sqrt(1+(ħt/mσ0²)²) in v1 and sigma_t_sq = σ0² + (ħ·dt/(m·σ0))² in v2.
findings.evidence: This is the same expression, and it is correct for the paper's own convention ψ∝exp(−x²/2σ²). Check of an evolving packet at σ0=2, t=7: norm 1.000000000000, <x²> = 8.12500000 = σt²/2, residual of i∂tψ + ½∂x²ψ is 1.3e−9 at |ψ|≈0.37 (finite differences). ħ and m are constructor arguments, not parameters; only σ0 is learned. The gradient with respect to log_sigma0 at initialisation ≈ −2.6e−3; all 4 heads start at σ0 = 2.

findings.claim: What the v2 envelope is as a function of distance: in v2 positions are integer token indices, t = d.
v1 Annex A: at small σ0 the kernel falls off sharply (local syntax); at large σ0 the head is a global filter over wide windows.
What the positional part of v2 is in ML terms; “Algebraic normalization … to bypass Softmax exponent logic”.
findings.evidence:
The whole layer with constant q·k gives attention rows E(d)²/ΣE² (max error 3e−8 at σ0 = 0.3, 2, 5). The layer with random weights in float64 matches softmax(log(Re²+Im²) + 2·log E(d)) with a causal mask: max|Δout| = 1.8e−8, the remainder explained by the 1e−9 epsilons.
So the positional part is a Toeplitz multiplicative prior E(i−j)² of fixed shape with one learnable scalar σ0 per head. Equivalently, it is an additive bias b(d) = −log(1+u²) − σ0²u²/(1+u²) on the logits 2·log|q·k*|. The normalisation A/ΣA is the same softmax of log A, i.e. the exponential has not gone anywhere; only the notation has changed.
Nearby the bias is quadratic: b ≈ −d²(1/σ0²+1/σ0⁴), for example at σ0=5, d=1: −0.0415 vs −0.0416. Far away it is logarithmic: b + 2·log d tends to a constant (−4.906 at σ0=0.3, −1.224 at σ0=2), i.e. the weight decays as 1/d².
ALiBi (a linear bias) fits poorly: the best line over d≤127 leaves a residual of 4.7–8.9 nats. The KERPLE log kernel −r1·log(1+r2·d) fits at σ0≤2: residual 0.04, 0.31 and 0.75 nats at σ0 = 0.3, 1, 2, r1 ≈ 2–2.8. At σ0≥5 it does not fit (2.9 and 8.3 nats): there it is a Gaussian window.

findings.claim: v1, section 2.1 and item 2 of the abstract: position is encoded by the phase e^{iωs}, an “exact, continuous equivalent to RoPE” in the position difference. Is this still in v2?
findings.evidence:
v2 has no ω, and positions do not enter q and k: the string 'omega' is in neither of the two v2 files. raw = Σ q·conj(k) with q = QR+iQI is a quantity that depends only on token content. Being complex gives only A ∝ s_re² + s_im², a sum of squares of two real bilinear forms.
Without the envelope and the mask the layer is permutation-equivariant: max|f(Px) − P·f(x)| = 3.6e−16 at σ0=e^20 vs 1.02 at σ0=2.
The reviewer's model (src/models.py, LM) has no positional embeddings. So in cvqiaa2 all position information is E(d) and the causal mask, and cvqiaa2-noenv is NoPE.
Positions in v2 are integer indices, in v1 0.1·index, so the σ0 of the two versions (2 vs 0.5 and 4) are not directly comparable.

findings.claim: The v2 letter: the discrete grid O(T²×N_grid) is replaced by a “native O(T²) calculation” of the same integral.
findings.evidence:
The v1 code with the grid (wavellm_fixed.py, 64 points on [−5,5]), as long as the packet fits into the grid, equals const·(c): the ratio to exp(−d²/4σt²) is √π·63/640 = 0.1745 with a deviation of 9.4e−4 at σ0=0.5. At σ0=4 the deviation is 1.4e−2 because of grid truncation.
v2 computes a different function: E = √2·(σ0/σt)·(c)². At the same σ0 and positions the behaviour is opposite. Example: σ0=0.5, T=128, under (c) the median is d=63 and the share on its own token is 0.009; in v2 the median is 0 and the share on its own token is 0.928.
So v2 is a new positional function, not a grid-free version of v1. The “fix of inverse dispersion” comes precisely from the new factor σ0/σt, not from σ0 becoming learnable.

findings.claim: The authors' tests set log_sigma0 = −12 and −15 “to confirm subnormal arithmetic is stable”.
findings.evidence: At these values σ0² = 3.8e−11 and 9.4e−14 are smaller than the 1e−9 epsilon inside sqrt and exp, and the formula changes. E(0) = 0.270 and 0.0137 instead of 1.414. E(1) = 5.3e−11 and 1.3e−13, so the weight of a neighbour relative to the own token is ~4e−20 and ~9e−23: the layer looks only at its own token. The test checks a degenerate regime in which the epsilons distort the formula, not the layer's working regime.

checks.correction: The conclusion is correct. Two refinements; they do not change the verdict. (1) The constant factor √2 in E cancels in the normalisation A/ΣA: A_ij = |s_ij|²·E², so E(0)>1 only proves that the formula is misnamed and does not affect the layer outputs (except relative to eps 1e-9). Only the shape of E(d) matters. (2) The phrase “it is a density” is imprecise. E/√2 does equal N(d;0,σt²)/N(0;0,σ0²), but it is not the density of the packet the code spreads. At σ0=2, d=5: E/√2 = 0.185. In the paper's convention |ψ(d,t)|²/|ψ(0,0)|² = 0.055. In the convention ψ∝exp(−x²/4σ²) with its own spreading law it is 0.090. So the formula is a hybrid: the density shape from one convention, the spreading law from another.
checks.evidence: r1_overlap.py: evolution is computed independently of the closed forms, with an exact FFT propagator exp(−ik²t/2) on 2^18 points. Maximum discrepancy with formulas (a) 2.9e−11, (b) 4.5e−12, (c) 1.2e−11, norm 1±1.2e−11. At σ0=2: d=5 gives |a|=0.2994, b=0.2096, c=0.5435, code 0.2610; d=50 gives 8.0e−3, ~0, 0.370, 1.55e−2. The identity E=√2(σ0/σt)c² holds with relative error ≤5.7e−14. E(0) in float64 with eps is 1.41421355. I checked the formula SpatialOverlap=exp(−(sQ−sK)²/4σ(t)²) and the real ψQ, ψK of width σ(t) against the rendered page 2 of the v1 PDF (v1_p2.png).

FFT evolution of both packets over t=d at σ0∈{0.3,1,2,5}, d≤50 gives the overlap exp(−d²/4σ0²) with error 4.5e−12, i.e. t drops out of the answer. Tail of (a) at σ0=0.3, d=50: FFT 0.05484 vs sqrt(2σ0²/d)·e^{−σ0²} = 0.0548. Plateau of (c) at σ0=0.3: 0.97775 for d from 5 to 50. On page 2 of v1 both packets have the same σ(t) and are written without the chirp.

checks.correction: The σ(t) law is correct. The figure “gradient with respect to log_sigma0 ≈ −2.6e−3” cannot be checked: it depends on a random input and a loss function that are not specified, and it says nothing about the formula.
checks.evidence: r4_units.py, FFT at σ0=2, t=7: norm 1.000000000000, <x²> = 8.12500000 = σt²/2. The v1 and v2 lines coincide algebraically: σ0²(1+(t/σ0²)²) = σ0²+(t/σ0)².

r2_shape.py, source lines executed in float32. The table matched completely, e.g. σ0=5: 1.41, 1.39, 1.3, 0.857, 0.234, 2.87e−05, 2.67e−06, 1.33e−07. E>1 at d≤1, 4, 16 for σ0 = 2, 5, 20. At σ0=20 E==0 from d=417, E²==0 from d=238. No non-increasing steps in float64 at d≤1e5 for any σ0. Tail coefficient 1.041 (σ0=√2), 1.318e−4 (σ0=5), 7.83e−85 (σ0=20).

checks.correction: The numbers line by line are correct. But two phrases, “the v1 pair (0.5 and 4) is ordered opposite to Annex A” and “σ0=4–4.5, the wide v1 head, is a window of 2–3 tokens”, plug the v1 σ0 into the integer positions of v2. The agent itself writes in phase-rotation-gone that such a comparison is invalid: in v1 positions are 0.1·k. If the v2 formula is computed in v1 units, the pair is ordered as Annex A says: σ0=0.5 gives 0.254 on its own token, a median of 2 tokens, a d≥32 share of 0.030; σ0=4 gives 0.027, a median of 19 tokens, a d≥32 share of 0.28. Correct wording: within v2 (integer positions) the d≥32 share is non-monotonic in σ0. A local maximum of 6.8e−3 at σ0≈1.29, a minimum of 2.6e−8 at σ0≈5.7, and the share rises above 6.8e−3 again only at σ0>16.4. The Annex A ordering holds only at the extremes: as σ0→0 the weight on the own token →1, as σ0→∞ the weight is uniform.
checks.evidence: r2_shape.py, T=128, weight E². On the own token: 0.988 (σ0=0.3), 0.928 (0.5), 0.651 (1), 0.410 (2), 0.201 (5). Share at d≥32: 1.75e−4, 1.08e−3, 5.73e−3, 6.62e−3 (1.41), 2.94e−3, 1.02e−6 (4), 4.60e−8, 2.57e−2 (20), 0.369 (50). Median d: 2 at σ0=4, 9 at σ0=20. A sweep of 2000 σ0 values from 0.2 to 100 gives a minimum of 2.58e−8 at σ0=5.71. Decomposition of the log weight at σ0=0.5, d=127: −12.461 and −0.250. TV distance to exp(−d²/σ0²): 7.7e−4 (σ0=20) and 1.2e−4 (σ0=50). r4_units.py: the v2 formula at positions 0.1·k (result above).

checks.correction: The equivalence is correct. There are four inaccuracies. (1) “The exponential has not gone anywhere, only the notation has changed” is an overstatement: any positive normalisation w/Σw is softmax(log w), so such a rewrite is tautological. The real change is that content enters as |s|², polynomially, rather than as e^s; this is the same substitution as in the born variant. (2) “Nearby the bias is quadratic, b≈−d²(1/σ0²+1/σ0⁴)” holds only for d≪σ0². At σ0≤1 no integer d≥1 falls into this region: b(1) = −4.913 vs −134.6 at σ0=0.3 and −1.193 vs −2.000 at σ0=1. The approximation works at σ0=2 (−0.296 vs −0.3125) and σ0=5 (−0.0415 vs −0.0416). (3) −1.224 at σ0=2 is the value at d=127, while the limit 4·lnσ0−σ0² is −1.2274. (4) The fit residuals depend on a criterion that is not stated. Least squares with the maximum residual over d≤127 gives for σ0 = 0.3/1/2/5/20: ALiBi 9.44/5.66/5.51/7.69/5.94 nats, KERPLE log kernel 0.09/0.47/1.13/2.67/6.64. The picture is the same, but the figures 0.04/0.31/0.75 are not reproduced this way.
checks.evidence: r3_layer.py, float64, random weights, σ0 = 0.3/1/2/5: max|layer − softmax(log|s|² + 2logE, causal mask)| = 4.7e−8 at an output scale of 1.07. The values of b(1) and b(127)+2ln127 are printed there too.

The string 'omega' is not in paper_v2_replacement.py or paper_v2_blueprint.py (the check returned False, False). With causal_mask=False and log σ0=20, max|f(Px)−P·f(x)| = 1.0e−15; at σ0=2, 0.61. In models.py the LM has no positional embeddings; RoPE exists only inside StandardAttention (the softmax and born variants); Analytical (cvqiaa2) has no positional encoding.

checks.correction: The main conclusion is correct: v2 is a new function, not v1 without the grid. The decomposition confirms that the inversion is removed by the factor σ0/σt. At σ0=0.5 the share on the own token: 0.0088 under the c² formula, 0.0100 with the doubled exponent alone, 0.920 with the σ0/σt factor alone, 0.928 in v2. The claim “the v1 code with the grid equals const·(c), deviation 9.4e−4 / 1.4e−2” is imprecise. In the actual v1 configuration (T=128, positions 0.1·k up to 12.7, grid [−5,5]) the equality const·(c) with the ratio exactly 0.17448 = √π·63/640 holds only for pairs where both packets are inside the grid. At σ0=0.5 there are 158 such pairs out of 8256 causal ones, at σ0=4 none. Over all pairs the ratio lies in 0.0000–0.1745 (σ0=0.5) and 0.0006–0.162 (σ0=4). The deviation figures from the finding are not reproduced under the stated setup.
checks.evidence: r3_layer.py, section 5 (FreeEvolutionQuantumAttentionHead from wavellm_fixed, grid_size=64, float64); r4_units.py (decomposition).

checks.correction: Worth adding: “subnormal arithmetic” does not arise in this test at all (see evidence).
checks.evidence: r3_layer.py. At log σ0 = −12 and −15: σ0² = 3.775e−11 and 9.358e−14, E(0) = 0.2697 and 0.01368, E(1) = 5.34e−11 and 1.32e−13, weight ratio (E1/E0)² = 3.9e−20 and 9.4e−23. The blueprint test configuration (log σ0=−15, B=2, T=128, seed 0): among 66048 non-zero A there are 0 subnormals, minimum A = 3.1e−35 (>1.18e−38). The diagonal carries ≥0.999999 of each row's mass, i.e. the attention layer acts as the identity map.

refute.missed: 1) Learned σ0. In results/train-cvqiaa2-seed0.json and train-cvqiaa2-seed0-lr0.003.json all 32 heads (16 per run) finished training with σ0 from 1.78 to 3.73. At these values and equal |s|: on the own token 0.26–0.44, d≤4 share 0.90–0.96, d≥32 share from 3.4e−6 to 4.5e−3. So all learned heads are local windows of 2–5 tokens. None reached σ0>16.4, where the distant weight grows again. At the initial σ0=2 the derivative of the d≥32 share with respect to log σ0 is −1.3e−2. Growing σ0 first lowers the distant weight by about 5 orders of magnitude, to 2.6e−8 at σ0≈5.7, so the “global” regime is separated from the starting point by a dip in the positional prior. The content term |s|² can compensate, but at σ0=5.7, d=32 it needs a factor in |s| of order e^8 (script r2_shape.py). 2) The factor √2, and any other constant factor in E, cancels in normalisation: E(0)>1 is an error in the formula's name, not in the layer outputs. 3) With causal_mask=False dt is clipped to 0, and every future key gets E=√2, like the own token: for query 0 the row of E over keys 0..4 is [1.414]×5. Without the mask the layer cannot distinguish the positions of future tokens. In the demo scripts and models.py the mask is on by default, so this does not affect the published runs. 4) The authors' test “subnormal arithmetic is stable” produces no subnormal numbers (0 of 66048) and checks a degenerate regime where the attention layer acts as the identity map. NaN cannot appear by construction, because there is no abs. All scripts and outputs were in the reviewer's working folder: r1_overlap.py, r2_shape.py, r3_layer.py, r4_units.py, their *.out and v1_p2.png.

found.summary: The v2 layer indeed no longer builds B×T×T×N_grid tensors. Peak memory compared with v1 drops 4.6 times, CPU time 13–15 times, memory growth is O(T²). But the claim of “computational parity with standard matrix attention” is not confirmed against any baseline. At T=2048 v2 saves 80 times more memory for backward than SDPA (60 times more at peak), 7.1 times more than plain softmax (3.8 times at peak), and 2.5 times more than born. In FLOPs it is 2.3× (attention kernel 2.5×); in single-thread CPU time, 2.3× plain softmax and 4.7× SDPA at T=1024. The authors' test 2 compares numbers counted by different methods. Counted the same way, v2's saved-for-backward is only 10–17% smaller than v1's, because the v1 grid tensors were never saved. The memory conclusion depends on the implementation, not on the formula: the same layer computed in query blocks with checkpointing saves 14.4 MB instead of 511 MB at T=1024 (SDPA level). In compute, at least 2× remains with any implementation. Caveats: the CPU was heavily loaded (load average 95–361, swap 22.1 of 22.5 GB in use), so wall-clock time is noisy, and the reliable figures are single-thread process CPU time. v1 at T=2048 was not run; its saved memory was counted on the meta device. I once ran `git status` in the repository by mistake; the contents of .git/index did not change (mtime 18:53).

findings.claim: “The layer now runs at computational parity with standard matrix attention”: memory
findings.evidence: One layer: B=4, d_model=128, H=4, CPU. Saved-for-backward in MB at T=1024 / 2048. Counted by storage, each storage once: sdpa 14.6/28.9, naive softmax 75.5/280.8, born 206.6/804.9, v1 580.2/2216.3 (2048 on meta), v2 511.4/2000.5. The reviewer's method (data_ptr, dtype, shape): sdpa 12.6/24.9, naive 139.5/536.8, the rest the same. v2 to sdpa: 40.7×/80.4× by the reviewer's method (35×/69× by storage). v2 to naive: 6.8×/7.1× by storage (3.7×/3.7× by the reviewer's method). v2 to born: 2.48×/2.49×. Peak live memory over forward+backward (torch.profiler, profile_memory) at T=1024/2048: sdpa 28.4/50.7, naive 201/789, born 460/1825, v2 765/3020, v1 3564/not run. v2/sdpa = 27×/60×, v2/naive = 3.8×, v2/born = 1.66×. There is no parity with SDPA or with an explicit T×T matrix.

findings.claim: “Computational parity with standard matrix attention”: FLOPs and time
findings.evidence: FlopCounterMode at T=1024, forward: sdpa/naive/born 2.684 GFLOP, v2 6.174 GFLOP (2.30×); forward+backward 8.05 vs 18.52 GFLOP. Elementwise passes over a B·H·T·T matrix (in units of one such tensor): v2 20.75 in forward + 34 in backward, naive 7+7, born 7.1+15; SDPA does not materialise the matrix. Single-thread process CPU time, median [q1–q3], 6 repeats, variants interleaved. T=1024: sdpa 77.8 [75–85], naive 159 [140–164], born 124 [114–131], v2 365 [334–391] ms, i.e. v2/sdpa 4.7×, v2/naive 2.3×, v2/born 2.9×. T=512: 27.1 / 38.4 / 32.0 / 84.1 ms, v1 1265 ms; v2 against them 3.1× / 2.2× / 2.6×. T=256: 10.6 / 12.3 / 10.4 / 24.6 ms, v1 324 ms. Wall clock on 6 threads at load average 95–361 (zoom, vitest, other agents' jobs): T=2048 sdpa 407, naive 1132, born 1570, v2 4673 ms, interquartile range up to 2×. Same direction, unreliable magnitude.

findings.claim: Test 2 in Blueprint: “Saved Autograd Tensors at Context 512: … (The old implementation required ~158 MB)”; Replacement: “✅ Grid-free O(T^2) execution confirmed”
findings.evidence: The authors' script prints 149.66 MB on CPU. 158 MB is the reviewer's figure, counted with deduplication. By the authors' own method (no deduplication) v1 at T=512 gives 180.23 MB. Counted the same way, the reduction is 17% (149.66 vs 180.23) or 15.5% (133.66 vs 158.21); at T=2048, 10% (2000.5 vs 2216.3). Saved-for-backward barely changed because the v1 grid tensors were not saved for backward. v2's gain is at peak: 903→196 MB at T=512. Test 2 does not measure the peak. The tests contain no comparison with standard attention. The line “O(T^2) confirmed” in Replacement is always printed: it is not a check but a print after a single measurement (42.234 MB at T=256 for the whole demo model). Backward packs in the authors' counter are 0, i.e. their figure is the forward pass without deduplication.

findings.claim: Task 2: how many B×H×T×T tensors v2 creates in forward and how many it saves for backward
findings.evidence: Counted via TorchDispatchMode at T=24 (B=4, H=4, d_head=32). Forward allocates 15 B×H×T×T float32 tensors: 4 bmm (QR·KRᵀ, QI·KIᵀ, QI·KRᵀ, QR·KIᵀ), add, div, sub, div, two mul for the envelope, two pow, add, masked_fill, div (A_normalized). On top of these: 11 tensors of 1×H×T×T (the envelope chain), 5 tensors of 1×1×T×T, 2 tensors of T×T (ones, tril) and a bool mask. Saved for backward: 6 B×H×T×T: raw_re, raw_im, Psi_re, Psi_im, A after masked_fill, A_normalized. On top of these: 6 tensors of 1×H×T×T, 2 float 1×1×T×T and a bool mask. Total 24·B·H + 24·H + 9 = 489 bytes per T². Check: the T² term at T=2048 is 1956.0 MiB, measured 2000.5; the remainder 5.9 → 11.4 → 22.4 → 44.5 MB doubles with T, i.e. it is linear. For comparison, saved: naive 1 B×H×T×T tensor and a bool mask (65 B/T²), born 3 tensors and a float mask (196 B/T²), SDPA 0, v1 528 B/T². The v2 backward allocates 20 B×H×T×T tensors and 26 tensors of 1×H×T×T.

findings.claim: «We have removed the massive B × T × T × N_grid tensor allocations»
findings.evidence: The v2 forward has no allocation of shape (B,T,T,64); v1 has 20. The largest allocation in v2 is one B·H·T·T tensor: 16/64/256 MB at T=512/1024/2048. In v1, 256/1024 MB at T=512/1024. Peak v1→v2: 232→52 (T=256), 903→196 (T=512), 3564→765 MB (T=1024), i.e. 4.6 times. Single-thread CPU time v1→v2: 324→24.6 and 1265→84.1 ms, 13–15 times.

findings.claim: «Replaces the discrete O(T² × N_grid) coordinate grid with a native O(T²) calculation»
findings.evidence: Growth of v2's saved-for-backward at each doubling of T: 3.67, 3.83, 3.91 (tending to 4). The T² term is exactly 489 B/T². This is the same class as naive (3.15, 3.49, 3.72) and born. SDPA grows 1.93, 1.97, 1.98: O(T) memory. So O(T²) for v2 is correct, but SDPA, the baseline for training, is linear in memory.

findings.claim: Task 5: matmuls and FLOPs per head against standard attention
findings.evidence: Derivation. Standard attention per head: QKᵀ gives T²·d MAC, AV another T²·d, total 2·T²·d. v2: four real QKᵀ-like matmuls of T²·d each and AV T²·d, total 5·T²·d, i.e. 2.5×. The minimum with the Gauss trick (3 real multiplications per complex one) is 4·T²·d, i.e. 2×. Projections per token: v2 6·d_model² (q_real, q_imag, k_real, k_imag, v, out) vs 4·d_model², i.e. 1.5×. FlopCounter confirms: bmm 16.11 vs 6.44 GFLOP for forward+backward at T=1024 (2.5×), mm+addmm 2.42 vs 1.61 (1.5×). For sdpa FlopCounter counts the full T² and ignores the causal saving.

findings.claim: Task 5: KV cache size per token and decoding cost of v2 against standard attention
findings.evidence: Result for d_model=128, fp32, per token and layer. Standard attention caches K and V: 2·128·4 = 1024 bytes. v2 caches KR, KI and V: 3·128·4 = 1536 bytes, 1.5 times more. v1 cached 2048 bytes. The envelope depends only on the integer distance and sigma0 and need not be cached; in decoding it is O(H·T) operations. Decoding one token per layer: in attention 5·T·d_model MAC vs 2·T·d_model (2.5×), in projections 6·d_model² vs 4·d_model². The v2 code has neither generate nor a KV cache, and WaveTransformerDemo has no decoding path, so the authors did not test this mode.

findings.claim: Task 5: number of attention parameters per layer
findings.evidence: Counted as sum(p.numel()). Standard attention from models.py (qkv without bias): 65,664. born: 65,664. v1: 45,312. v2: 99,076 (6 Linear 128×128 layers with bias and 4 log_sigma0 values). That is +50.9%, and against the standard variant with bias (66,048), 1.50×. At the same d_model v2 is one and a half times heavier than standard attention.

findings.claim: Is v2's O(T²) memory unavoidable (a measure of whether memory parity is achievable at all)
findings.evidence: Each output row depends only on its own row of scores, and normalisation is per row and needs no max. So the layer can be computed in query blocks with checkpointing. My implementation with the published layer's weights: at T=512 and block 64 the output difference is 0.0, the relative gradient difference 8.8e-7, saved 7.4 MB instead of 133.7. At T=1024 and block 128: difference 0.0, gradient difference 1.3e-6, saved 14.4 MB instead of 511.4 (SDPA 14.6 by storage). Memory parity is achievable by engineering, with a fused kernel or blocks, but the authors did not do it. The price is recomputing the forward pass. The FLOPs gap of at least 2× remains with any implementation.

findings.claim: Task 3: consequences for what fits in memory
findings.evidence: v2's saved = 24·B·H·T² + 24·H·T² + 9·T² bytes plus O(T) terms. A layer of this size at T=2048: 2.0 GB saved and 3.0 GB peak; 4 such layers need at least 8 GB for attention alone, SDPA about 0.1 GB. At T=8192 the formula gives 489·8192² = 30.6 GiB saved per layer: on a 24 GB GPU not even one layer fits. Naive 4.1 GiB, SDPA about 0.1 GB. In the reviewer's training (ctx 128, batch 32, 4 layers) v2 saves about 52 MB per layer, which fits easily. found.summary: The v2 layer itself in float32 with σ0 near its initial value works correctly. Causality holds bit for bit, gradients are finite and match finite differences, and context 8192 runs without NaN. It breaks in three places. In float16, from dt≥256 the envelope becomes zero, and from dt≥362 forward gives NaN. In bfloat16 the positions torch.arange(T, dtype=bf16) are rounded, and that alone makes the output differ from float32 by 19% at T=512 and 50% at T=2048. At small σ0 (log σ0 ≤ −5) the layer degenerates into attention on its own token only, and q, k and log_sigma0 stop receiving gradient. The authors' own stability tests (log σ0 = −15 and −12) run the layer exactly in this degenerate regime, so their “PASS” tests the identity map. Separately: Born weights do not see the sign or phase of the score, so a query cannot tell key k from −k. In addition, as σ0 grows, access to distant tokens drops by 10+ orders of magnitude in the range σ0≈5–15 before rising again.

findings.claim: Outputs at early positions do not depend on future tokens (values and gradients)
findings.evidence: float64 and float32, log σ0 ∈ {ln2, −12, +5}, B=3, T=48. For all 47 cut points the future x were replaced by randn·100: max|Δy_past| = 0.000e+00, 0 points without a bitwise match. Gradient of early outputs (t<20) with respect to future inputs: max = 0.000e+00, with respect to past ones 1.3–2.4. My reimplementation matches the layer with diff 0.0.

findings.claim: NaN or inf in a future token does not affect past positions
findings.evidence: NaN or inf in the input at t=10 (T=16) gives NaN in all 16 rows, including t<10: A@V produces 0·NaN. The standard F.scaled_dot_product_attention(is_causal=True) with NaN in value at t=10 also gives NaN in all 16 rows, so the defect is general, not specific to v2.

findings.claim: Position 0 and rows where all scores are zero
findings.evidence: An ordinary position 0: weight 1 on itself, all correct. If a query has q=0 (q/k biases zeroed, x_t=0 at t=0 and t=3), the row weight sums in head0 = [0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, …]: the output at t=0 and t=3 is bitwise equal to out_proj.bias, the attention contribution is silently zeroed, and the gradient with respect to x_0 has norm 0.0. Softmax in such a row would give a uniform average.

findings.claim: The test “CPU Gradient Stability … subnormal” (log σ0 = −15 in blueprint, −12 in replacement) confirms the layer's stability
findings.evidence: Both of the authors' scripts print PASSED on CPU. But under their test conditions the mean weight on the own token is 0.999903 (−15) and 1.000000 (−12), the maximum weight on any other token 4.3e-20 and 1.1e-17: the layer behaves as an elementwise linear map, with no attention. The log_sigma0 gradient there is 1e-2…3e-2 and 1e-5…6e-5, while at σ0=2 on the same data it is 1.2–9.4. NaN does not appear because the forward pass has no torch.abs(complex), not because the working regime was tested.

findings.claim: The gradient with respect to log_sigma0 is informative and allows σ0 to be learned
findings.evidence: Autograd matches a central finite difference (float64) to 4–5 digits for log σ0 from −15 to +10; at σ0=2 it is −9.07 (for comparison mean|grad q_real.w| = 2.17). But at log σ0 ≤ −5 the weight on itself = 1.0000 at any input scale (0.1, 1, 3). The log σ0 gradient drops to 3.2e-8 at −8 and 1.3e-5 at −5, and so do the q/k gradients (mean|grad q_real.w| 6.2e-6 at −8). Training only log σ0 towards a teacher (Adam lr 0.05, 300 steps) recovers the targets −1.20, +0.69 and +3.40 from starts −5…+10. From starts −15 and −12 Adam drives σ0 even lower, to −18.3, −20.7 and −21.9 (loss 9e-4…2.5e-2): σ0 acts as an output multiplier through the eps leak. From +20 the value does not move at all (gradient 1.07e-14, finite difference 0). With SGD, without Adam's normalisation, the starts −5 and +10 would also get stuck.

findings.claim: The normalisation A/(ΣA+1e-9) gives weights summing to 1
findings.evidence: env(0)² = 2σ0²/(σ0²+1e-9) is proportional to σ0² when σ0 < 3e-5 (log < −10.4). LayerNorm input, scale 1, T=128: the share of rows with weight sum < 0.99 is 0.0076 at −16, 0.39 at −18 and 1.0 at −20 (attention output norm 0.695 of exact normalisation). At scale 0.1: 0.99 at −15 and 0.46 at −14. Norm of the attention part of the output (C=64, T=64): 29.6 at −15, 20.7 at −20, 2.6 at −22, 0 at ≤ −35. At σ0=2 there is no shrinkage at scales 0.003…1 if the q/k biases are non-zero. With zero biases A grows as the fourth power of the input scale: at scale 0.01, 99.9% of rows have sum < 0.99; at 0.003, 100% have sum < 0.5.

findings.claim: The learned σ0 is bounded
findings.evidence: log_sigma0 is not bounded by anything: no clamp, no parametrisation. The only thing pulling it is the weight decay 0.01 in AdamW from train.py (towards log σ0 = 0). In float32 forward gives NaN at log σ0 ≥ 44.5 (σ0² = inf) and ≤ −104 (σ0 = 0). The log_sigma0 gradient becomes NaN at log σ0 ≤ −26 (T=64), and the attention part of the output is silently zeroed at ≤ −35. Scanned −15…−45 and ±44…89.

findings.claim: As σ0 grows, the envelope smoothly widens access to distant tokens
findings.evidence: Result: the exponent dt²/(2σ0²+2dt²/σ0²) tends monotonically to σ0²/2 as dt→∞, so the tail ≈ √2·σ0²/dt·exp(−σ0²/2). Share of envelope² mass at dt>64 (T=1024, uniform content): σ0=1: 3.5e-3; 2: 1.75e-3; 5: 1.3e-10; 8: 1.3e-15; 10: 2.0e-14; 20: 6.6e-6; 30: 2.4e-3; 100: 0.36; 1000: 0.91. At the initial σ0=2 the mean weight at dt>64 is 0.0022–0.0025 at T=1024, 4096 and 8192. To get long-range context a head must pass through a dip of 10+ orders of magnitude at σ0≈5–15.

findings.claim: float32 at T = 1024, 4096, 8192: no NaN/inf, underflow is harmless
findings.evidence: B=1, d=16, 1 head, σ0 ∈ {3e-7, 2, 20, 148}: forward and backward are finite at all T; at T=8192 a run takes 5–14 s, peak RSS 4.6 GB. Share of zeros in A (lower triangle): σ0=20, 59/89/94%; σ0=148, 0/40/67%. This is the Gaussian tail, and the diagonal keeps the row sum ≥ 0.13. At σ0 ≤ 10 the envelope does not become zero at any dt ≤ 8191; the first zero: σ0=14.4 at dt=1748, σ0=20 at dt=417, σ0=148 at dt=2151. Weight sum < 0.99 only at σ0=3e-7: 13 rows at T=8192 (min rowsum 2.4e-9).

findings.claim: The layer works after model.half()
findings.evidence: In float16 eps 1e-9 becomes 0.0. dt**2 = inf at dt ≥ 256, so the envelope = 0 beyond 256 and distant tokens are silently cut off. 2·σt² overflows at dt ≥ 362 (σ0=2), giving inf/inf = NaN. T=128: error 8.0e-4, no NaN. T=512: 150 NaN rows, the first at 362, backward not finite. T=2048: 1686 NaN rows. At T=128 forward gives NaN in all rows for log σ0 ≤ −9 (σ0² goes to 0, giving 0/0) and for ≥ 5.6 (σ0² overflows). Backward is not finite already at −8 and −5. The cvqiaa2-noenv variant (log σ0 = 20) has σ0 = inf in fp16, giving NaN.

findings.claim: pos = torch.arange(T, dtype=x.dtype) and dt are exact in bfloat16
findings.evidence: bf16: at T=128 positions are exact. At T=512 there are 385 distinct positions out of 512, max position error 1, dt wrong in 43.8% of pairs i>j, 190 pairs of past tokens with dt=0 (treated as the current token). At T=2048: 641 of 2048, position error up to 4, dt up to 9, wrong in 83.5% of pairs, 4657 pairs with dt=0. No NaN. Relative output error against fp32: 7.3e-3 (T=128), 0.19 (T=512), 0.50 (T=2048). An fp32 layer with only the positions rounded to bf16 gives 0.191 and 0.497: all of the error comes from positions. Fix: compute pos and dt in float32 regardless of x.dtype.

findings.claim: torch.autocast on CPU with bfloat16
findings.evidence: Module and input in fp32, autocast cpu/bf16. T=128/512/2048: no NaN, gradients (including log_sigma0) finite, relative error 5.7e-3 / 5.9e-3 / 5.8e-3. Inside the LM from models.py under autocast the layer input stays float32, so positions are exact.

findings.claim: The Born weight |q·conj(k)|² can replace softmax(q·k)
findings.evidence: A constructed example, d_head=4, flat envelope (log σ0=20): the query's scores = (+5, −5, 0, 0). Born gives weights [0.5, 0.5, 0, 0], softmax [0.987, 4.5e-5, 6.7e-3, 6.7e-3]. The key values are +1 and −1, so the layer output is 0.0, softmax's 0.99. The weights do not change under a random phase rotation of each key and each query, including k → −k (max|ΔW| = 1.7e-16). For softmax max|W(s) − W(−s)| = 0.87. Shifting the score through a key bias partly restores the order (c=5: [0.8, 0, 0.2]) but lowers the contrast (c=20: [0.5, 0.18, 0.32]).

findings.claim: The option causal_mask=False gives meaningful bidirectional attention
findings.evidence: dt = clamp(i−j, min=0), so all future tokens get dt=0 and the full envelope² = 2.0 regardless of distance. In row 32 of 64 at σ0=2, future tokens carry 92.7% of the envelope² mass. In a causal LM this branch is not used.

checks.evidence: s1_causal.py (own run, seed 7, B=2, T=40, C=32, H=4; float32 and float64; log σ0 ∈ {ln2, −12, +5}): for all 39 cut points the future x were replaced by randn·50, max|Δy_past| = 0.000e+00, 0 cuts without a bitwise match. Gradient of outputs t<15 with respect to inputs t≥15: max = 0.000e+00, with respect to past ones 1.4–3.2.

s1_causal.py: NaN and inf in x[t=10] (T=16) give NaN in all rows 0–15. F.scaled_dot_product_attention(is_causal=True) with NaN in v[t=10]: also rows 0–15. With NaN only in k[t=10] SDPA spoils only rows 10–15, and in v2 masked_fill removes the NaN from A, so in both the leak goes only through V (0·NaN in A@V). The defect is general; severity info is correct.

s1_causal.py: q/k biases zeroed, x_0 = x_3 = 0. Weight sums in head0 = [0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]; y[0] and y[3] are bitwise equal to out_proj.bias; the gradient norm with respect to x_0 and x_3 is 0.0, with respect to x_1 3.40. Reason: d|s|²/ds = 2s = 0 at s=0, so there is no gradient through k_0, v_0 either. The situation is artificial (with non-zero biases q=0 has probability 0), so severity minor is correct.

checks.correction: The mechanism is confirmed: at small σ0 attention works only on itself, the q, k and log σ0 gradients vanish, Adam from −15 and −12 goes even lower, and SGD from −5 and +10 does not move (the checker did not measure this; I did, and it was confirmed). The inaccuracies are these. (1) Degeneration starts earlier than −5: the mean weight on itself is ≥ 0.9999 already at log σ0 = −3 (σ0 = 0.05), and 0.996 at −2. (2) Autograd agrees with the finite difference at −8 to only 3 digits (3.2192e-8 vs 3.2152e-8), not 4–5. (3) “Recovers from starts −5…+10” is not always true: for the target −1.20 the start +10 ended at −1.35 (loss 1.2e-4). (4) Severity major is overstated in practice: in all three cvqiaa2 training runs on TinyStories the learned σ0 lie in 1.78–4.95, far from the degeneration region (σ0 ≤ 0.05). checks.correction: The numbers for dt>64 reproduce exactly, and there is indeed no monotonic widening. But the depth and position of the dip depend on the chosen distance D. At D=16 the dip is only about two orders: 7.6e-3 at σ0=2 and a minimum of 1.1e-4 at σ0=5. At D=256 it is deeper than 50 orders and spans σ0 from 5 to 50 (4.3e-57 at σ0=15). refute.missed:
1) The authors' “subnormal stability” test creates no subnormal numbers at all. At log σ0 −15 (blueprint) and −12 (replacement) their count in env, Psi and A is 0, the minimum non-zero A 3.4e-35 and 3.9e-28. In fp32 subnormals appear in v2 only at σ0 ≈ 12–55: at T=512, 58187 elements of A at log σ0 = 2.5, 29129 at 3.0, 9 at 4.0, and the gradients there are finite. Where v2's backward actually breaks in fp32 (the log_sigma0 gradient is not finite at log σ0 ≤ −25), the authors did not test. Scripts s2_authors.py, s10_bound.py.
2) Born normalisation has no temperature. The weights do not change when q is scaled, nor when all keys are scaled together. Multiplying the weights and biases of q_real and q_imag by 0.1, 10 or 100 changes W by at most 6e-7, and the mean row entropy stays 1.277. For softmax q×10 lowers the entropy from 3.154 to 1.323. The layer cannot sharpen attention through the norm of the query, only through directions; the contrast between two keys is the square of the ratio of |q·k̄|, i.e. it grows polynomially, not exponentially. Script s9_sign.py.
3) Context for low precision. fp16 breaks only under model.half(): CPU autocast fp16 works (error 7.2e-4, backward finite at T=2048). Softmax SDPA in pure fp16 and bf16 works at all T with errors of 2.5e-4–3.0e-4 and 2.0e-3–2.5e-3, so v2's error in pure bf16 (0.19 and 0.50) is a property of v2 specifically. CUDA was not tested. Script s7_lowprec.py.
4) Practical significance of the “trap” and the “dip”. In results/train-cvqiaa2-seed0.json, train-cvqiaa2-seed0-lr0.003.json and train-cvqiaa2-seed1-lr0.003.json the learned σ0 of all 16 heads lie in 1.78–4.95. No head entered the degeneration region (σ0 ≤ 0.05) or crossed the dip (σ0 ≥ 15). Heads that grew to 3.7–4.95 became more local: the amplitude of the distant tail 2σ0⁴e^{−σ0²} drops from 0.59 at σ0=2 to 2.8e-8 at 4.95.
All scripts were in the reviewer's working folder.

found.summary: Version 2 does not fix the previous layer; it replaces it with a different, simpler one. From v1, the complex V, the phase rotation e^{iωs}, reading the modulus |ΣAV| and the fixed narrow and wide heads are gone. What remains is square normalisation (Born rule) over two real scores and a distance factor with a learnable width. Its formula is derived nowhere: it does not match the paper's own formula from section 2.2, and at dt=0 it gives 1.414, i.e. more than 1. What v2 really fixes: the two typos (together with the complex tensors), NaN on CPU (0 of 20 steps in the real model), the grid and the loop over heads; σ0 became learnable. Against v1 memory is 12–21% lower and CPU time about 9 times lower. But memory is still 3.4–3.7 times more than explicit softmax and 11–41 times more than sdpa, so the claimed “parity with standard attention” is not confirmed. The v2 materials contain no training (AdamW is created but step() is never called), no baseline model for comparison and no control. The NaN test passes just as well on the old form with torch.abs, and there are no subnormal numbers in it. The line “O(T^2) confirmed” is printed without any check. Not addressed: quality against softmax, the 50% memory saving from Annex C, the KV cache, photonic O(1) and physical causality. The v1 paper PDFs are byte-identical (SHA-256), so the published false claims still stand. Both v2 documents are unedited output of a Gemini chat.

findings.claim: The letter and the code comments present v2 as a fix of the same layer (“Patch”, “Fixes old .mtheH bug”, “Corrected Dispersion Dynamics”).
findings.evidence: Comparison of the v2 code with the v1 papers (sections 2.1–2.3, Annex A–C, the code in both papers). KEPT: Q and K as pairs of real projections. raw_re and raw_im equal exactly the Re and Im of QK† (allclose=True). So |Ψ|² = env²·(s1²+s2²), where s1=[QR,QI]·[KR,KI] and s2=[QR,QI]·[−KI,KR] are two real bilinear scores. The formula σt² = σ0² + (ħdt/mσ0)². Row normalisation |Ψ|²/(Σ+1e-9). An explicit tril mask. GONE: the phase rotation e^{iωs} and the learnable ω (section 2.1, “an exact analogue of RoPE”): a grep for omega, cos, sin, torch.complex, abs( finds nothing. Complex V. Reading the modulus |ΣA V| (section 2.3). The overlap formula from section 2.2. Fixed heads σ0 = 4.0/0.5 (Wave-Transformer) and 4.5/0.6 (main paper). Input positions 0.1×index. Slicing the input across heads. NEW: a learnable log σ0, initially 2.0 for all heads. The factor sqrt(2σ0²/σt²). Eps terms inside sqrt and exp. Bias in the projections. Heads computed in one matrix operation. Layer parameters: 45,312 (v1) → 99,076 (v2), softmax 65,664. In essence it is real Born attention with two scores, multiplied by a distance kernel; the text of the v1 paper describes a different architecture.

findings.claim: The replacement script: “CV-QIAA PATCH HARNESS: REPRODUCIBLE EVALUATION OVERHAUL”; WaveTransformerDemo “mimicking original evaluation architecture”; “✅ Grid-free O(T^2) execution confirmed”.
findings.evidence: A grep finds no call to .step() in any of the v2 scripts: the optimiser is created, but the model is not trained. There is no data, no loss curve, no baseline model and no control. The finding of section 2 of the review (the demo checks nothing) is not fixed: the demo is simply removed. The demo has one attention layer without residual, LayerNorm or FFN (grep is empty), while the v1 WaveLLM has two pre-LN blocks with FFN and residual. The line “O(T^2) confirmed” is printed unconditionally after one size, T=256 (output 42.234 MB), so scaling cannot be checked from it. Both scripts were run twice: the outputs match.

findings.claim: The letter: “deriving the closed-form analytical coordinate-space integral of the wave-packet overlaps”; docstring: “integrating wave-packet fields symbolically”.
findings.evidence: There is no derivation in any PDF. A closed form was already in v1 section 2.2: exp(−dt²/4σ(t)²). It numerically matches the integral of the paper's own normalised packets (σ0=2, dt=5: 0.54348 and 0.54348; σ0=4, dt=20: 0.087246 and 0.087246). The v2 formula, sqrt(2σ0²/σt²)·exp(−dt²/2σt²), gives something else: σ0=0.5, dt=1, 0.305 vs 0.943; σ0=4, dt=127, 6.7e−5 vs 0.0195. Nor does it match the exact overlap of a freely spread packet with the original shifted one (0.548 and 1.4e−7 at the same points). At dt=0 v2 gives 1.4142 > 1, while the overlap of normalised states is at most 1 by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

findings.claim: The letter: “The layer now runs at computational parity with standard matrix attention”.
findings.evidence: Memory saved for backward, counted by the reviewer's method (B=4, d=128, 4 heads), T = 256/512/1024, MB. v2: 36.45/133.66/511.44. Explicit softmax: 10.88/37.62/139.5. sdpa: 3.33/6.41/12.56. v1: 46.19/158.21/580.25. So v2 takes 3.35–3.67 times more than explicit softmax and 11–41 times more than sdpa, and only 12–21% less than v1. CPU time (forward+backward; training on MPS ran in parallel, so the measurements are noisy). First run: v2 27/97/283 ms, explicit softmax 20/114/127, sdpa 10/28/44. Second run, ratios: v2 to explicit softmax 1.38/3.46/2.57, v2 to sdpa 2.40/3.06/5.60. On paper: v2 has 4 matrix multiplications per head for the scores and 1 for A·V, 5·T²·d_head operations in total vs 2 for softmax (2.5 times more), and 6 d×d linear layers vs 4.

findings.claim: The letter: “removed the massive B×T×T×N_grid tensor allocations”, O(T²) instead of O(T²·N_grid). This also answers section 7 of the review (heads computed in a loop).
findings.evidence: The v2 code has neither x_grid nor 4D×grid tensors; the largest tensors are of size B×H×T×T. Heads are computed in one matrix operation. On CPU v2 is faster than v1: 27.4 vs 233.7 ms at T=256 (8.5 times) and 97.2 vs 935.5 ms at T=512 (9.6 times). However, in the v2 materials themselves the only evidence is a single memory number for a single size.

findings.claim: Test 2 in blueprint: “Track saved tensors exactly like cv-qiaa-eval hooks”; prints 149.66 MB and “The old implementation required ~158 MB at this scale due to grid generation”.
findings.evidence: The counting in the test differs from the reviewer's: duplicates are not excluded and backward is included. The same way, v1 gives 180.23 MB; by the reviewer's method v2 gives 133.66 and v1 158.21. The comparison 149.66 vs 158 mixes two methods. With the same method the saving is 16–17%, while the authors' own output suggests about 5%. The explanation “due to grid generation” contradicts README section 4 (grid tensors are not saved for backward) and the measurement: v2 without a grid still saves 133.66 MB. Ordinary softmax (37.62 MB) is not in the test.

findings.claim: Test 1: “Explicitly force parameters into subnormal bounds to trigger a crash if unstable” and “confirm subnormal arithmetic is stable”; outputs “✅ PASSED” and “Absolute stability achieved on CPU”.
findings.evidence: The same test on v2 with |Ψ|² computed the old way again, torch.abs(complex)**2, also passes: NaN=False both in the blueprint test (log σ0=−15) and in the replacement test (log σ0=−12). So the test cannot detect the error it was written for. There are zero subnormal numbers in envelope, env² and A at both values. The envelope at dt=0 is determined by eps 1e-9: 0.0137 and 0.270 instead of 1.414. Attention in this regime is almost the identity: the mean share of weight on itself is 0.9999 and 1.0000. “Absolute stability” is also wrong: NaN in gradients at log σ0 ≤ −25, NaN already in forward at log σ0 ≥ 45; the NaN-free range is −20…44. In training from the initial log 2 such values are practically unreachable.

findings.claim: The letter: “CPU NaNs Fixed ... P = Re² + Im²”; section 6 of the review.
findings.evidence: The reviewer's model (4 layers) with cvqiaa2, B=32, T=128, 20 AdamW steps on CPU: 0 of 20 steps with NaN or inf in gradients. In v1 after the very first step there is NaN in 139 of 172 tensors (diagnose.json). This is the same fix the reviewer checked in diagnose.py, check 4. The v2 materials contain no evidence: their test is uninformative, see test1-no-power.

findings.claim: The letter: “Syntax Errors Resolved ... eliminating the invalid .mtheH calls”; comment in the demo: “Correct targets memory layout mismatch by substituting reshape”.
findings.evidence: Both v2 scripts run (2 runs, same output). The .mtheH error disappeared because there are no complex tensors any more; it was an AttributeError, not a syntax error. reshape is in the demo, where targets is a separate tensor rather than a slice, so the fix is not exercised. The letter does not mention the second typo. The v1 paper PDFs with both errors are unchanged in the authors' folder (see paper-unchanged).

findings.claim: The letter: “σ0 now explicitly learned per-head ... without hardcoded boundary truncation bugs”; docstring: “Resolves inverted dispersion physics via per-head learnable log_sigma0”.
findings.evidence: σ0 is learned: it is a Parameter, d/dlog σ0 = −6.46 at log σ0=0, and over 20 steps σ0 moves from 2 to 1.94. Truncation at the edges disappeared because the grid was removed, not because σ0 is learnable. Learnability of σ0 by itself does not change the formula: the distance profile was changed by the new envelope formula. At small σ0 the gradient almost vanishes: −4.7e−7 at log σ0=−10 and 8.9e−6 at −5. A head whose σ0 has shrunk is left with attention on itself only.

findings.claim: Annex A: the narrow head handles local syntax, the wide one the topic. The letter: the “inverted wave-packet dynamics” are fixed.
findings.evidence: Query at position 127, equal semantic scores, share of positional weight env² on the 5 nearest characters. Under the v1 formula: σ0=0.5 → 0.040 (uniform weight would give 0.039), σ0=4 → 0.682. Under v2: σ0=0.5 → 0.990, σ0=4 → 0.885. The reversed order at short distances is gone. But any σ0 ≤ 16 leaves at least 33% on the 5 nearest. The share at dt ≥ 64 changes non-monotonically with σ0: 2.2e−3 at 1.41, 9.6e−4 at 2, 9.6e−8 at 4, 2.1e−15 at 8, 5.0e−8 at 16, 0.155 at 64 (uniform weight would give 0.5). To become wide, a head needs σ0 ≳ 64 ≈ T/2, and the path from the initial 2 goes through σ0 4–16, where distant tokens are suppressed even more. In the reviewer's parallel runs (results/train-cvqiaa2-seed0*.json) σ0 after training is 1.78–3.73: 0.90–0.96 on the 5 nearest, at most 1.5e−3 beyond 64. All heads are local; none is wide.

findings.claim: The last sentence of blueprint proposes training on TinyStories “to confirm that our evaluation loss now beats standard Softmax attention”; section 3 of the review.
findings.evidence: There is not a single quality measurement in v2. There are only the reviewer's parallel runs: they are not part of the v2 materials, one seed each, taken from results/*.json. cvqiaa2 0.9465 vs softmax 0.9175 at lr 3e-3; 0.9854 vs 0.9723 at lr 1e-3. The gap shrank from 0.12 (v1) to 0.03, but v2 does not beat softmax. Meanwhile v2 has 950,544 parameters (396,304 in attention) vs 816,896 (262,656). Training 239–267 s vs 131 s on MPS.

findings.claim: The author's post: thanks for “several critical errors in the code and mathematics, as well as false claims”, “the files with the corrected code are at the same link”. The letter accepts as correct the remarks on memory, speed, inverse dynamics and NaN on CPU.
findings.evidence: Only two PDFs with code were added. The paper PDFs and the README are byte-identical in the 10:20 and 18:49 snapshots and in the repository: SHA-256 d0ca70cc… (Wave-Transformer), 4cf94ba8… (main paper), 8153fdfd… (README). They still contain K.mtheH, targets.view, “stable 50% activation memory reduction” (Annex C), photonic O(1), the narrow and wide heads of Annex A, physical causality from Annex B, “Born-Rule Cross Entropy” and the demo as proof of convergence. Not one false claim is withdrawn or named. The letter is silent on the review's main conclusion (quality worse than softmax), on the demo, on the 50%, on the KV cache and on photonics.

findings.claim: Annex C: on GPU a “stable 50% activation memory reduction” (section 4 of the review).
findings.evidence: v2 does not address this; the claim remains in the paper. v2 saves 3.35–3.67 times more than explicit softmax and 11–41 times more than sdpa (T=256–1024), see parity-memory-time.

findings.claim: The table from the post: KV cache “O(T·d) with 50% saving” (section 7 of the review).
findings.evidence: v2 has neither generate() nor a cache (a grep for generate and cache is empty). Counted on paper at d_model=128, float32: the v2 cache per token and layer is KR, KI and V, 3·128·4 = 1536 B. In ordinary attention K and V take 1024 B; in v1 the complex K and V take 2048 B. So v2 is 50% larger than ordinary attention, not 50% smaller.

findings.claim: Annex B: causality is ensured physically, through wave propagation.
findings.evidence: In v2 causality is still held only by the explicit tril mask. Because of clamp(dt, min=0), future keys get the envelope at dt=0, i.e. 1.4142, the largest value among all keys (σ0 = 0.5, 2 and 4). Before the mask, the envelope gives the future the largest weight.

findings.claim: Annex C and the post: a photonic implementation with O(1) time and memory.
findings.evidence: v2 does not address this; there is neither a chip nor a simulation. Moreover, v2 removed the phase rotation and the reading of the modulus |·| on which the photonic explanation relied (WDM, photodetector, Born rule).

findings.claim: The nature of the v2 documents: not a claim about the method, but important for how to read them.
findings.evidence: Blueprint opens with “You can send them the following breakdown”: Gemini is addressing the user, not the reviewer. The reviewer is referred to in the third person (“executed directly within their environment”). Below the code is “Use code with caution.”, a Gemini interface caption. It ends with the question “Would you like me to adapt this patch into a fully working script that replaces paper_wavellm.py ... or should we focus on running a local training test ... to confirm that our evaluation loss now beats standard Softmax attention?”. The second PDF, “The Fully Functional Reviewer Replacement Script”, is the first option of that question; the second option, training, was not done, although its result is presumed in the very wording. There is no signature. Emoji ✉️, 🛠, ✅, ❌. The AttributeError is called a syntax error, σ0 is called dispersion. The 158 MB figure is taken from the reviewer's table and explained incorrectly. The two v2 layers are functionally identical: output difference 0.0.

checks.evidence: Rerun (arch.py). raw_re and raw_im match the Re and Im of QK† (allclose True). Layer parameters: v1 45,312, v2 99,076, softmax 65,664. Whole models (LM): 950,544 / 396,304 for v2 vs 816,896 / 262,656 for softmax. Checked against the pages of the main paper's PDF. Section 2.1: Q, K and V are multiplied by e^{iωs}. Section 2.3: Out = W^O·|ΣA V|. In the paper's code σ0 = 4.5 and 0.6 (Wave-Transformer 4.0 and 0.5), positions 0.1×index, the input is sliced across heads. None of this is in v2. A small inaccuracy: a grep for “abs(” and “complex” finds these words in v2 comments (“torch.abs() CPU NaN crash”), but there are no calls in the code.

grep '\.step\(' finds nothing in either v2 script (exit 1). A grep for LayerNorm, ffn, residual, generate and cache is also empty. In the code the line “✅ Grid-free O(T^2) execution confirmed” is printed with no condition after a single measurement (42.234 MB at T=256). The demo is an Embedding, one attention layer and lm_head. The v1 WaveLLM has two pre-LN blocks with FFN and residual.

Section 2.2 on page 2 of the PDF: ψ_Q and ψ_K are normalised, the overlap equals exp(−(s_Q−s_K)²/4σ(t)²). My numbers (envelope.py, float64): at σ0=0.5, dt=1 v2 gives 0.3049, v1 0.9429; at σ0=4, dt=127, 6.72e−5 vs 1.95e−2. I derived analytically the exact overlap of a freely evolved packet with the original shifted one: √2·(4+τ²)^(−1/4)·exp(−d²/(σ0²(4+τ²))), τ=t/σ0²; numerical integration agrees. At the same points it gives 0.5475 and 1.446e−7. At dt=0 v2 gives 1.4142. Caveat: the constant factor √2 cancels in row normalisation; only the shape of the curve affects attention. But the shape is different too: v2/v2(0) at σ0=0.5, dt=1 is 0.216, v1's 0.943. The conclusion does not change.

Memory by the reviewer's method reproduced to the byte (mem.py). v2: 36.453 / 133.656 / 511.438 MB, explicit softmax: 10.875 / 37.625 / 139.5, sdpa: 3.328 / 6.406 / 12.562. refute.missed: 1. The main gap is that the long-range conclusion depends on the init. With the published sigma0=2, gradient descent stays on the near side of the valley. Repeat-24 stays at chance at lr 3e-3 and 1e-2 (0.031 and 0.033, with sigma0 1.9-2.1). With sigma0 initialised at 40, the same layer learns repeat-24 to 0.729 in 600 steps, against 0.481 for noenv. It sets itself up as layer 1 local (sigma0 about 11) and layer 2 wide (20-43). There is no sigma0-init ablation on TinyStories, so 'the envelope is a local window' is proven for the authors' init only. The authors' letter says sigma0 is learned 'so the network can optimize localization'. The result refutes that from their init, but they can answer 'change the init'. A cheap fix is a cvqiaa2 run with sigma0 init of 40 or 160 at lr 3e-3. 2. The 'Adam budget' argument is wrong: Adam steps can exceed lr (2.51x measured), and the observed travel was 1.45x the total lr. 3. The authors claim 'computational parity'; the timing evidence for that is confounded by load: the same-config born run took 158 s once and 459 s another time. 4. The authors' letter expects v2 to beat softmax on TinyStories. The finished pairs so far show the opposite at both lrs, by about 0.011 nats at 1e-3 and about 0.024 at 3e-3, with 2-3 seeds each. That is still partial. 5. noenv is not position-free: through the causal mask it reaches 0.48 on repeat-24. Scripts and outputs are in agents/harness-refute: check_a.py (with check_a.out), repro.py (repro_softmax.out), sanity2.py (e1-e5 *.out) and grad0.py.
